items.title: Chuck Mancuso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 10, 2013
items.q: He was using a little too much of Wynton

ctx.x: Oh he was — the stuff was great. I mean Sudhalter makes a great case in his book, you know, about the whites. And even Nick LaRocca — you know there are more Italians down in New Orleans at the turn of the twentieth century, at the beginning of the twentieth century, than there were in New York City, even though we all came through Ellis Island. Because the French owned it, the Spanish, and then the French a second time. Catholic. And in New Orleans a similar atmosphere, weather. And there were all these Italians…

stuff, of Gunther Schuller. Schuller had it right. He was using a little too much of Wynton and, at the time Gary Giddons, but especially Stanley Crouch. I call him Stanley Grouch. I brought him up here. What a pain in the neck, but what a funny guy.
Really. A pain in the neck and a funny guy?
